Extend a layout

Source: R/nodes.R
add_right.Rd

add_right() places plots to the right of a layout, add_below() places them below.

Usage

add_right(layout, ..., horizontal_align = NULL, vertical_align = NULL)

add_below(layout, ..., horizontal_align = NULL, vertical_align = NULL)

Arguments

layout

A layout, ggplot or grob.

...

ggplots (including tidyplots), grobs or layouts. Lists are spliced, so the output of stretch_y() can be passed directly. In row() and column(), NULL is ignored; in grid(), NULL leaves an empty cell.

horizontal_align, vertical_align

Alignment of the resulting row or column, i.e. where it places its direct plots (see row()). To align the plots inside a nested row or column, set the alignment on that row or column instead. NULL keeps the current alignment when appending, and uses the default ("left", "bottom") when wrapping.

Value

A layout.

Details

If the layout is already a row (for add_right()) or a column (for add_below()), the plots are appended to it. Otherwise, including for grids, the layout is wrapped in a new row or column together with the new plots.

Examples

p1 <- dummy(name = "p1", color = "#0072B2")
p2 <- dummy(name = "p2", color = "#D55E00")
p3 <- dummy(name = "p3", color = "#009E73", height = NA)
p4 <- dummy(name = "p4", color = "#E69F00", width = NA)

row(p1, p2) |>
  add_right(p3) |>
  add_below(p4)
